PROGRAMME AT EINDHOVEN AIRPORT,PILOTS OF MODE S EQUIPPED ACFT WITH
ADS-B FUNCTIONALITIES WHEN OPERATING ON THE GROUND SHALL: A)SELECT
AUTO MODE AND THE ASSIGNED MODE A CODE OR B)IF AUTOMODE IS NOT
AVAILABLE, SELECT ON (E.G.XPDR) AND THE ASSIGNED MODE A CODE. -FROM
THE REQUEST FOR TOWER PUSH-BACK OR TAXI,WHICHEVER IS EARLIER -AFTER
LANDING,CONTINUOUSLY UNTIL THE ACFT IS FULLY PARKED IN ITS STAND.
-WHEN THE ACFT IS FULLY PARKED, FLT CREW SHALL SELECT STBY.
1.1.2.WHENEVER THE ACFT IS CAPABLE OF REPORTING ACFT IDENTIFICATION
(I.E.CALLSIGN USED IN FLT), THIS SHOULD BE ENTERED (THROUGH THE FMS
OR THE TRANSPONDER CONTROL PANEL) AT THE TIME OF THE REQUEST FOR
TOWED PUSH-BACK OR TAXI, WHICHEVER IS EARLIER. 1.1.3.AIR CREW MUST
USE THE ICAO DEFINED FORMAT TO ENTER THE ACFT IDENTIFICATION.
1.1.4.TO ENSURE THAT THE PERFORMANCE OF SYSTEMS BASED ON SSR FREQ
(INCLUDING AIRBORNE TCAS AND SSR RADARS) IS NOT COMPROMISED, TCAS
SHOULD NOT BE SELECTED BEFORE RECEIVING CLEARANCE TO LINE UP, AND
SHOULD BE DESELECTED AFTER VACATING THE RWY.

THIS NOTAM, FLIGHT CREW INCLUDES CABIN CREW

1. FLIGHT CREW ARRIVING IN MAURITIUS AND WHO:
A. HAS DEPARTED FROM, TRAVELLED TO, OR TRANSITED THROUGH THE

THE PRECEDING TWENTY-ONE (21) DAYS, EXCEPT AS PROVIDED IN PARAGRAPHS

2. MAURITIAN FLIGHT CREW AND AIR MAURITIUS FOREIGN CREW WHO HAVE
DEPARTED FROM, TRAVELLED TO, OR TRANSITED THROUGH THE DEMOCRATIC
REPUBLIC OF CONGO OR SOUTH SUDAN DURING THE PRECEDING TWENTY-ONE (21)
DAYS SHALL BE SUBJECT TO QUARANTINE, MEDICAL ASSESSMENT AND
MONITORING BY THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND WELLNESS.
3. THE ABOVE RESTRICTION DOES NOT APPLY TO QUICK TURNAROUND FLIGHT
CREW WHO DO NOT DISEMBARK IN MAURITIUS.
4. THE ABOVE RESTRICTION DOES NOT APPLY TO TRANSIT POSITIONING FLIGHT
CREW WHO ONLY TRANSIT IN THE TERMINAL BUILDING SUBJECT TO FLIGHT CREW
NOT INVOLVED IN SERVING FLIGHTS TO COUNTRIES MENTIONED AT PARAGRAPH
1A DURING THE PRECEDING TWENTY-ONE (21) DAYS. IF ATTENDING RESTRICTED
COUNTRIES, FLIGHT CREW INVOLVED SHALL BE PLACED IN ISOLATION ROOM
PRIOR TO DEPARTURE.
5. ALL FLIGHT CREW TRAVELLING TO MAURITIUS SHALL BE REQUIRED TO
COMPLETE AND PRESENT THE PRESCRIBED ALL-IN-ONE HEALTH DECLARATION
FORM PRIOR TO BOARDING.
6. AIRCRAFT OPERATORS SHALL ENSURE STRICT COMPLIANCE WITH THE ABOVE
REQUIREMENTS REGARDING FLIGHT CREW AND ENSURE THAT AIR MAURITIUS
FOREIGN CREWS OPERATING IN MAURITIUS HAVE THE NECESSARY VALID
PERMITS.
7. ISOLATION AND PUBLIC HEALTH RESPONSE PROCEDURES FOR SUSPECTED
CASES SHALL BE IMPLEMENTED IN COORDINATION WITH THE MINISTRY OF
HEALTH AND WELLNESS.
8. THIS NOTAM REMAINS IN FORCE UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE.

HEALTH AND WELLNESS.
3. NON-CITIZENS WHO HAVE DEPARTED FROM, TRAVELLED TO, OR TRANSITED
THROUGH THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO OR SOUTH SUDAN DURING THE

A.A RESIDENCE PERMIT
B.AN OCCUPATION PERMIT

D.A STUDENT PERMIT

F. A PREMIUM VISA.
SUCH PASSENGERS SHALL, UPON ARRIVAL, BE SUBJECT TO QUARANTINE,
MEDICAL ASSESSMENT AND MONITORING BY THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND
WELLNESS.

COMPLETE AND PRESENT THE PRESCRIBED ALL-IN-ONE HEALTH DECLARATION
FORM PRIOR TO BOARDING.
5.AIRCRAFT OPERATORS SHALL IMMEDIATELY NOTIFY THE RELEVANT MAURITIAN
AUTHORITIES OF ANY SUSPECTED CASE OF EBOLA VIRUS DISEASE ON BOARD AND
SHALL COMPLY WITH ALL PUBLIC HEALTH DIRECTIONS ISSUED BY THE MINISTRY
OF HEALTH AND WELLNESS.
6.AIRCRAFT OPERATORS SHALL ENSURE STRICT COMPLIANCE WITH THE ABOVE
REQUIREMENTS. PASSENGERS WHO DO NOT MEET THE CONDITIONS SPECIFIED
HEREIN SHALL NOT BE ACCEPTED FOR CARRIAGE TO MAURITIUS.
7.ISOLATION AND PUBLIC HEALTH RESPONSE PROCEDURES FOR SUSPECTED CASES
SHALL BE IMPLEMENTED IN COORDINATION WITH THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND
WELLNESS.
8.THIS NOTAM REMAINS IN FORCE UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE.

WASHINGTON, DC. ENFORCEMENT ACTIONS:

INTERCEPTED, AND/OR DETAINED AND INTERVIEWED BY FEDERAL, STATE, OR

C. ANY PERSON WHO KNOWINGLY OR WILLFULLY VIOLATES THE RULES
CONCERNING OPERATIONS IN THIS AIRSPACE MAY BE SUBJECT TO CRIMINAL
PENALTIES UNDER 49 USC SECTION 46307.
D. THE U.S. GOVERNMENT MAY USE DEADLY FORCE AGAINST AN AIRCRAFT
OPERATING IN THE DC SFRA, INCLUDING THE DC FRZ, IF IT IS DETERMINED
THAT THE AIRCRAFT POSES AN IMMINENT SECURITY THREAT.
E. A VISUAL WARNING SIGNAL (VWS) FOR COMMUNICATING WITH VFR
AIRCRAFT, INCLUDING DOD, LAW ENFORCEMENT, AND AEROMEDICAL
OPERATIONS, IS DEPLOYED AND IS OPERATING WITHIN THE WASHINGTON DC
SPECIAL FLIGHT RULES AREA (SFRA), INCLUDING THE FLIGHT RESTRICTED

ZONE (FRZ). THE SIGNAL CONSISTS OF HIGHLY FOCUSED RED AND GREEN

A. APPLICATION OF DEFINITIONS IN 14 CFR SECTION 93.335:
1. A DC SFRA FLIGHT PLAN DOES NOT FULFILL THE REQUIREMENTS FOR
VISUAL FLIGHT RULES (VFR).
2. A DC FRZ FLIGHT PLAN IS REQUIRED FOR VFR OPERATIONS IN THE DC

B. ADDITIONS TO REQUIREMENTS IN 14 CFR SECTION 93.339 - DC SFRA:
1. AIRCRAFT OPERATING IN THE DC SFRA MUST BE EQUIPPED WITH AN

6. AIRCRAFT DEPARTING AIRPORTS WITHIN THE DC SFRA WITH LIMITED

AS SOON AS FEASIBLE, NORMALLY WITHIN 2NM OF THE DEPARTURE POINT.
7. PATTERN WORK OPERATIONS AT UN-CONTROLLED AIRPORTS WITHIN THE DC
SFRA (BUT NOT WITHIN THE DC FRZ) MUST BE CONDUCTED IN ACCORDANCE
WITH 14 CFR SECTION 93.339 (C) AND THE PROCEDURES SPECIFIED IN THE
MOST CURRENT POTOMAC TRACON LETTER TO AIRMEN (LTA) ON THE SUBJECT.
THE LETTER CAN BE FOUND AT: HTTPS://NOTAMS.AIM.FAA.GOV/NOTAMSEARCH/
(SEARCH LOCATION PCT).
(A) ALL PILOTS WHO INTEND TO CONDUCT VFR TRAFFIC PATTERN WORK AT AN
AIRPORT WITHIN THE DC SFRA (NOT WITHIN THE DC FRZ) WHICH DOES NOT
HAVE AN OPERATING CONTROL TOWER OR WHEN THE CONTROL TOWER IS CLOSED
MUST: (1) INCLUDE ?PATTERN? IN SFRA FLIGHT PLAN REMARKS. (2) PRIOR
TO DEPARTURE, CONTACT POTOMAC TRACON VIA TELEPHONE NUMBER SPECIFIED
IN THE LTA TO OBTAIN TRANSPONDER CODE AND ADVISE TRACON OF INTENT TO
ZDC SECURITY INSTRUCTIONS, WASHINGTON, DC.
 THIS NOTAM
CONDUCT PATTERN WORK. WASHINGTON, DC. (3) INFORM ATC OF INTENT TO
CONDUCT PATTERN WORK PRIOR TO CHANGING TO COMMON TRAFFIC ADVISORY
FREQUENCY (CTAF) .
(B) UPON COMPLETION OF PATTERN WORK, PILOTS MUST CONTACT POTOMAC
TRACON VIA TELEPHONE NUMBER SPECIFIED IN THE LTA TO ADVISE PATTERN
WORK IS COMPLETE.
8. OPERATIONS BY UNMANNED AIRCRAFT SYSTEMS (UAS), INCLUDING MODEL
AIRCRAFT (HOBBYIST OR RECREATIONAL USE ONLY), CIVIL AND COMMERCIAL
OPERATIONS, AND PUBLIC OPERATIONS, ARE ONLY AUTHORIZED WITHIN THE DC
SFRA, EXCLUDING THE DC FRZ, IF IN COMPLIANCE WITH THE SEPARATE FAA
NOTAM, WHICH PRESCRIBES UAS-SPECIFIC OPERATING REQUIREMENTS IN THE
DC SFRA.
9. ALL TESTING OF ADS-B OUT ON AIRCRAFT OR GROUND VEHICLES
IN THE DC SFRA IS PROHIBITED.

 WASHINGTON,
DC. THIS NOTAM CANCELS FDC 4/1783
TO PROVIDE SPECIAL SECURITY INSTRUCTIONS FOR UNMANNED AIRCRAFT
OPERATIONS (UAS) IN THE WASHINGTON DC METROPOLITAN AREA SPECIAL
FLIGHT RULES AREA (SFRA), INCLUDING THE WASHINGTON DC METROPOLITAN
AREA FLIGHT RESTRICTED ZONE (FRZ). ADDITIONALLY, THIS NOTAM
SUPPLEMENTS THE DC SFRA, INCLUDING THE DC FRZ FDC NOTAMS WITH
SPECIAL SECURITY INSTRUCTIONS, INCLUDING OPERATING REQUIREMENTS,
THAT ARE SPECIFIC TO UAS OPERATIONS, INCLUDING OPERATIONS BY
RECREATIONAL OPERATORS, CIVIL (INCLUDING COMMERCIAL), AND PUBLIC
OPERATORS, IN THE DC SFRA PURSUANT TO 14 CODE OF FEDERAL REGULATIONS
(CFR) SECTIONS 93.335, 93.337, 93.339, 93.341, AND 99.7, AND 49
UNITED STATES CODE (USC) SECTION 40103(B)(3).
SECTION I. SPECIAL NOTES ON UAS OPERATIONS IN THE DC SFRA:
A. THE FAA HAS ESTABLISHED THE DC SFRA, INCLUDING THE DC FRZ,
PURSUANT TO 49 USC 40103(B)(3). PERSONS OPERATING UAS IN THE DC SFRA
WHO DO NOT ADHERE TO THE PROCEDURES PRESCRIBED BY 14 CFR SECTIONS
93.335, 93.337, 93.339, 93.341, AND 99.7, AND THE FOLLOWING
UAS-SPECIFIC SUPPLEMENTAL SPECIAL SECURITY INSTRUCTIONS MAY FACE
RESPONSE AND ENFORCEMENT ACTIONS AS DESCRIBED IN 14 CFR 93.333 AND
DC SECURITY INSTRUCTIONS, WASHINGTON, DC. THIS NOTAM FLIGHT
RESTRICTED ZONE (FRZ) FDC NOTAMS.
B. UAS OPERATIONS ARE PROHIBITED IN THE DC FRZ UNLESS AN AIRSPACE
WAIVER IS GRANTED IN ACCORDANCE WITH SECTION V, B. BELOW.
C. UAS OPERATORS WHO DO NOT COMPLY WITH APPLICABLE AIRSPACE
RESTRICTIONS ARE WARNED THAT PURSUANT TO 10 U.S.C. SECTION 130I AND
6 U.S.C. SECTION 124N, THE DEPARTMENT OF DEFENSE (DOD) , THE
DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY (DHS) OR THE DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE
(DOJ) MAY TAKE SECURITY ACTION THAT RESULTS IN THE INTERFERENCE,
DISRUPTION, SEIZURE, DAMAGING, OR DESTRUCTION OF UNMANNED AIRCRAFT
DEEMED TO POSE A CREDIBLE SAFETY OR SECURITY THREAT TO PROTECTED
PERSONNEL, FACILITIES, OR ASSETS.
SECTION II. OPERATING REQUIREMENTS FOR DC SFRA (RECREATIONAL
AIRCRAFT UAS OPERATIONS):
ALL RECREATIONAL AIRCRAFT UAS OPERATIONS ARE PROHIBITED WITHIN THE
DC SFRA UNLESS IN COMPLIANCE WITH ALL OF THE REQUIREMENTS LISTED
BELOW. REFER TO SECTION VI OF THIS NOTAM FOR THE APPLIED DEFINITION
OF RECREATIONAL AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS.
A. THE UAS IS REGISTERED AND MARKED AS REQUIRED BY THE FAA. REFER TO
INSTRUCTIONS PROVIDED AT
HTTPS://WWW.FAA.GOV/UAS/GETTING?STARTED/REGISTER?DRONE.
B. THE UAS WEIGHS LESS THAN 55 LBS, INCLUDING ALL ADDED EQUIPMENT
(SUCH AS CAMERAS) ATTACHED TO THE AIRCRAFT.
C. OPERATIONS MUST REMAIN AT OR BELOW 400 FEET ABOVE GROUND LEVEL
(AGL) UNLESS ISSUED A SIGNIFICANT GOVERNMENTAL INTEREST (SGI) WAIVER
ISSUED BY THE SYSTEM OPERATIONS SUPPORT CENTER (SOSC)
9-ATOR-HQ-SOSC?FAA.GOV
D. OPERATIONS MUST REMAIN WITHIN VISUAL LINE OF SIGHT OF THE
OPERATOR AND IN COMPLIANCE WITH THE FOLLOWING:
1. OPERATIONS MUST BE CONDUCTED UNDER VISUAL METEOROLOGICAL
CONDITIONS (VMC).
2. OPERATIONS MUST NOT BE CONDUCTED DURING NIGHT AS DEFINED IN 14
CFR SECTION 1.1.
3. FLIGHTS UNDER SPECIAL VISUAL FLIGHT RULES (SVFR) ARE NOT
AUTHORIZED.
E. OPERATIONS MUST COMPLY WITH ALL RESTRICTIONS AND LIMITATIONS
UNDER 49 USC 44809(A), (B), AND (C), EXCEPTION FOR LIMITED
RECREATIONAL OPERATIONS OF UNMANNED AIRCRAFT.
F. OPERATIONS MUST NOT INTERFERE WITH AND MUST GIVE WAY TO MANNED
AIRCRAFT.
G. RECREATIONAL AIRCRAFT UAS OPERATIONS ARE PROHIBITED IN THE DC
FRZ.
SECTION III. OPERATING REQUIREMENTS FOR DC SFRA (CIVIL, INCLUDING
COMMERCIAL, UAS OPERATIONS):
ALL CIVIL, INCLUDING COMMERCIAL, UAS OPERATIONS ARE PROHIBITED
WITHIN DC SFRA UNLESS IN COMPLIANCE WITH 14 CFR PART 107 OR THE
OPERATOR'S APPLICABLE FAA GRANT OF EXEMPTION PURSUANT TO 49 USC
SECTION 44807, AND FAA CERTIFICATE OF AUTHORIZATION OR WAIVER (COA).
REFER TO SECTION VI OF THIS NOTAM FOR THE APPLIED DEFINITION OF
CIVIL, INCLUDING COMMERCIAL, UAS OPERATIONS.
SECTION IV. OPERATING REQUIREMENTS FOR DC SFRA (PUBLIC UAS
OPERATIONS):
ALL PUBLIC UAS OPERATIONS ARE PROHIBITED WITHIN DC SFRA, UNLESS IN
COMPLIANCE WITH THE OPERATOR'S APPLICABLE CERTIFICATE OF
AUTHORIZATION (COA) OR WAIVER OR OPERATING UNDER 14 CFR PART 107.
REFER TO SECTION VI OF THIS NOTAM FOR THE APPLIED DEFINITION OF
PUBLIC UAS OPERATIONS.
SECTION V. ADDITIONAL GENERAL OPERATING REQUIREMENTS AND GUIDANCE
FOR DC SFRA (ALL TYPES OF UAS OPERATIONS):
A. UAS OPERATIONS IN THE DC SFRA MUST NOT PENETRATE RESTRICTED
AREAS, PROHIBITED AREAS, OR TEMPORARY FLIGHT RESTRICTIONS (TFR).
RESTRICTED AND PROHIBITED AREAS ARE DEPICTED ON CHARTS AVAILABLE
THROUGH THE FAA. REFER TO
WWW.FAA.GOV/AIR?TRAFFIC/FLIGHT?INFO/AERONAV. INFORMATION ON CURRENT
TFR'S CAN BE OBTAINED AT HTTP://TFR.FAA.GOV.
B. UAS OPERATIONS IN THE DC SFRA MUST NOT PENETRATE THE DC FRZ. UAS
OPERATIONS ARE PROHIBITED IN THE DC FRZ UNLESS SPECIFICALLY
AUTHORIZED VIA THE TSA/FAA AIRSPACE WAIVER PROCESS. CERTAIN
COMMERCIAL AND PUBLIC UAS OPERATIONS ARE ELIGIBLE TO REQUEST
AIRSPACE WAIVERS TO OPERATE IN THE DC FRZ. APPLICATION GUIDELINES
CAN BE FOUND AT:

SECTION VI. DEFINITIONS:
A. RECREATIONAL AIRCRAFT UAS: UAS MUST MEET THE REQUIREMENTS
PRESCRIBED BY 49 USC 44809, TO QUALIFY AS A RECREATIONAL AIRCRAFT,
WHICH IS USED EXCLUSIVELY FOR RECREATIONAL PURPOSES. UAS USED FOR
COMMERCIAL ACTIVITY DO NOT QUALIFY AS RECREATIONAL AIRCRAFT.
B. CIVIL, INCLUDING COMMERCIAL UAS: CIVIL UAS OPERATIONS GENERALLY
COMPRISE FLIGHTS CONDUCTED BY PRIVATE SECTOR ENTITIES FOR COMMERCIAL
PURPOSES. REFER TO 14 CFR PART 107 OR 49 USC SECTION 44807, FOR
ADDITIONAL DETAILS ON UAS OPERATIONS THAT ARE ADDRESSED BY SECTION
III OF THIS NOTAM.
C. PUBLIC UAS: PUBLIC UAS OPERATIONS GENERALLY INCLUDE GOVERNMENTAL
OPERATIONS, INCLUDING DEPARTMENT OF DEFENSE (DOD) AND NATIONAL GUARD
(NG) FLIGHTS. REFER TO 49 USC SECTION 40102(A) (41), WHICH PROVIDES
THE DEFINITION OF ?PUBLIC AIRCRAFT? AND 49 USC SECTION 40125
PROVIDES THE QUALIFICATIONS FOR PUBLIC AIRCRAFT STATUS.

CLEARANCE PROCEDURES. DUE TO REGIONAL AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL
AUTOMATION SYSTEM COMPATIBLY PROBLEMS THE FOLLOWING MODIFICATION
WERE MADE TO WESTBOUND OCEANIC FLIGHT CLEARANCE AND RECLEARANCE
PROCEDURES IN THE NORTH ATLANTIC REGION ON MAY 11, 2009. THESE
PROCEDURES ARE ONLY APPLIED WITHIN THE SHANWICK, GANDER, AND NEW
YORK AREA CONTROL CENTERS AND CONTINUE IN FORCE AS FOLLOWS:

LONGITUDE 67 WEST WILL BE CLEARED TO THE FIRST NAMED FIX IN THE NEW
YORK OCA THAT IS SPECIFIED IN THE AIRCRAFT'S FILED FLIGHT PLAN,
FOLLOWED BY THE PHRASEOLOGY - VIA FLIGHT PLANNED ROUTE TO
DESTINATION.
AIRCRAFT THAT WILL PROCEED SOUTH OF LATITUDE 20 NORTH AND EAST OF
LONGITUDE 60 WEST  WILL BE CLEARED TO THE LAST SET OF COORDINATES
SPECIFIED IN THE AIRCRAFT'S FILED FLIGHT PLAN PRIOR TO LATITUDE 20
NORTH FOLLOWED BY THE PHRASEOLOGY - VIA FLIGHT PLANNED ROUTE TO
DESTINATION.
AIRCRAFT THAT HAVE BEEN TAKEN OFF THEIR FLIGHT PLANNED ROUTE WILL
BE RECLEARED TO A FIX SPECIFIED IN THE AIRCRAFT'S FILED FLIGHT PLAN
FOLLOWED BY THE PHRASEOLOGY VIA FLIGHT PLANNED ROUTE TO DESTINATION.
IT IS IMPERATIVE THAT OPERATORS FILE FLIGHT PLANS (FPL) AND FLIGHT
PLAN CHANGE (CHG) MESSAGES THROUGH THE NEW YORK OCEANIC CTA/FIR USE

BEGINNING ON 5 FEBRUARY 2013 AT 1200Z, NEW YORK CENTER WILL MODIFY
THE PROCEDURES THAT ARE USED TO ISSUE OCEANIC CLEARANCES TO
EASTBOUND AIRCRAFT ENTERING MINIMUM NAVIGATION PERFORMANCE STANDARD
(MNPS) AIRSPACE. THESE PROCEDURES ONLY APPLY TO AIRCRAFT ENTERING
THE NEW YORK CENTER OCEANIC CTA FROM A FAA FACILITY. THE PURPOSE OF
THIS NOTAM IS TO EXPLAIN THESE CHANGES.
NORTH ATLANTIC (NAT) DOCUMENT 007, TITLED GUIDANCE CONCERNING AIR
NAVIGATION IN AND ABOVE THE NORTH ATLANTIC MNPS AIRSPACE IS A
GUIDANCE DOCUMENT PUBLISHED BY ICAO TO ASSIST USERS IN THE PROPER
PROCEDURES TO BE USED WHEN OPERATING IN THE NAT. CHAPTER 5 OF
DOCUMENT 007, TITLED OCEANIC ATC CLEARANCES, IS THE CHAPTER TO WHICH
THESE CHANGES PERTAIN.
THERE ARE THREE COMPONENTS TO AN OCEANIC CLEARANCE. THEY ARE ROUTE,
ALTITUDE AND SPEED. IT IS THE DELIVERY METHOD OF THESE THREE
COMPONENTS WHICH IS CHANGING. BEGINNING ON 5 FEBRUARY 2013, THE FAA
WILL CONSIDER THE AIRPORT CLEARANCE WHICH AN AIRCRAFT RECEIVES ON
THE GROUND AT ITS DEPARTURE AERODROME TO BE THE ROUTE PORTION OF THE
OCEANIC CLEARANCE. ALTITUDE AND SPEED ASSIGNMENT WILL OCCUR PRIOR TO
ENTRY INTO THE NEW YORK CENTER OCEANIC CTA. AS IS THE CURRENT
OPERATING PROCEDURE, UNSOLICITED EN-ROUTE ROUTE, ALTITUDE OR SPEED
CHANGES MAY OCCUR DUE TO CHANGING TRAFFIC SITUATIONS. AT ALL TIMES,
THE LAST ASSIGNED ROUTE, ALTITUDE AND SPEED ARE TO BE MAINTAINED AND
SHOULD BE CONSIDERED YOUR NEW OCEANIC PROFILE. HAVING RECEIVED ALL
THREE COMPONENTS, THE REQUIREMENT TO RECEIVE AN OCEANIC CLEARANCE
WILL HAVE BEEN MET.
FOR EXAMPLE:
AN AIRCRAFT HAS FILED AN FPL FROM MDSD TO EDDF. THIS WOULD TAKE THE
FLIGHT FROM THE SANTO DOMINGO FIR, THROUGH THE MIAMI FIR AND THEN
THE NEW YORK FIR BEFORE ENTERING SANTA MARIA. THE AIRPORT CLEARANCE
PROVIDED ON THE GROUND AT MDSD WOULD FULFILL THE ROUTE REQUIREMENT
OF THE OCEANIC CLEARANCE. ONCE AIRBORNE AND IN THE MIAMI FIR, FINAL
SPEED AND ALTITUDE ASSIGNMENT WILL BE GIVEN AFTER THE FLIGHT IS
COORDINATED BETWEEN MIAMI AND NEW YORK.
IF A ROUTE, SPEED OR ALTITUDE CHANGE EN-ROUTE IS DESIRED, THEN
AIRCRAFT SHOULD MAKE A REQUEST FROM THE ATC UNIT IN WHICH THEY ARE
OPERATING. AT ALL TIMES, THE LAST ASSIGNED ROUTE, ALTITUDE AND SPEED
ARE TO BE MAINTAINED.
TRACK MESSAGE IDENTIFICATION NUMBER (TMI) CONFIRMATION FOR AIRCRAFT
FILING AN ABBREVIATED CLEARANCE IN LIEU OF THE TRACK COORDINATES
WILL BE ACCOMPLISHED PRIOR TO REACHING THE TRACK ENTRY POINT.
USERS ARE REMINDED OF THE REQUIREMENT TO FILE AN FPL AND ANY
SUBSEQUENT CHANGES WITH NEW YORK OCEANIC AT KZWYZOZX, ALONG WITH ANY
OTHER ATC FACILITIES THAT MAY REQUIRE SUCH FILING.

WELL AS WITH INTERNATIONAL LAW AND ALSO REFUSES TO COORDINATE WITH
THE ONLY COMPETENT AUTHORITY WITHIN ATHINAI FIR, THE HASP.

A4808/26 (260829 EUECYIYN OCT 2026) OVERLAP AREAS OF NATIONAL

COINCIDES WITH ATHINAI FIR, AS MENTIONED IN GREEK COORDINATION
MESSAGE 220934 LGACYAYC OCT 2026, THROUGH THE JRCC PIRAEUS WHICH IS
THE ONLY COMPETENT AUTHORITY TO COORDINATE SAR SUPPORT MISSION
ACTIVITIES, AS REFERRED TO IN THE TURKISH NOTAM REQUEST MESSAGE
131900 LTAAYNYX OCT 2026.
MOREOVER, TURKIYE, IGNORING HCAA'S COORDINATION MESSAGE, NOT ONLY
DISREGARDS THE SAFETY OF THE GENERAL AIR TRAFFIC WITHIN ATHINAI FIR
BUT ALSO CAUSES DISRUPTION TO THE CIVIL AVIATION BY REQUESTING
LONG-TERM RESERVATION OF AIRSPACE AND BY BLOCKING MOST ECONOMIC
FLIGHT LEVELS, THUS COMPROMISING EFFICIENCY AND REGULARITY OF
INTERNATIONAL CIVIL AVIATION TRAFFIC.
CONSEQUENTLY, THE AREAS AS REQUESTED ARE NOT AVAILABLE.
FOR THE ABOVE MENTIONED REASONS THE TURKISH NOTAM A4808/26 (260829
EUECYIYN OCT 2026) IS NULL AND VOID AND NOT APPLICABLE TO ATHINAI FIR

4.2 'AIRPORT PROCEDURES IN REDUCED VISIBILITY CONDITIONS (RAVP)'
REDUCED VISIBILITY PROCEDURES APPLY WHENEVER CONDITIONS ARE SUCH
THAT ALL OR PART OF THE MOVEMENT AREA CANNOT BE VISUALLY MONITORED
BY ATS PERSONNEL. A REDUCTION IN AIRPORT CAPACITY IS TO BE EXPECTED
DUE TO INCRESEAD SPACING BETWEEN SUCCESSIVE ARRIVING AIRCRAFT AND
RESTRICTIONS APPLIED TO GROUND MOVEMENTS.
4.2.1 VISIBILITY CONDITION 2 (PART OF THE MOVEMENT AREA CANNOT BE
VISUALLY MONITORED BY ATS PERSONNEL)
THE SIMULTANEOUS PRESENCE OF MORE THAN ONE AIRCRAFT IS NOT PERMITTED
IN THE PORTION OF MANOEUVRING AREA NOT VISIBLE TO ATC PERSONNEL.
4.2.2 VISIBILITY CONDITION 3 (THE ENTIRE MOVEMENT AREA CANNOT BE
VISUALLY MONITORED BY ATS PERSONNEL)
THE SIMULTANEOUS PRESENCE OF MORE THAN ONE AIRCRAFT IS NOT PERMITTED
IN THE MANOEUVRING. FOLLOW-ME MANDATORY FOR TAXIING.
4.2.3 VISIBILITY CONDITION 4 (RVR EQUAL OR LESS THEN 75 M)
VISIBILITY CONDITION 3 PROCEDURES APPLIED
4.3 'TRAINING ACTIVITIES'
STARTING FROM RVR VALUE EQUAL TO OR LESS THAN 1500M AND/OR IN
CONDITIONS OF REDUCED VISIBILITY, THE TRAINING FLIGHT ACTIVITY IS
SUSPENDED.

 DERNIERS MOIS (EXPERIENCE RECENTE EN VOL OU SUR SIMULATEUR DE
 VOL (FSTD)).

 CONDITIONS A) OU B) SUIVANTES:
A) DETENIR LA QUALIFICATION DE VOL EN MONTAGNE,
B) DETENIR L'AUTORISATION D'ACCES PERMETTANT D'UTILISER
 L'AERODROME APRES AVOIR SUIVI UNE FORMATION THEORIQUE AU SOL ET
 PRATIQUE EN VOL SUR UN SIMULATEUR DE VOL (FSTD) SUR LES
 SPECIFICITES DE L'AERODROME ET DE SON ENVIRONNEMENT.
 CETTE AUTORISATION EST SPECIFIQUE AU TYPE OU A LA CLASSE
 CONSIDEREE POUR LES AVIONS AYANT UNE MASSE MAXIMALE CERTIFIEE AU
 DECOLLAGE DE PLUS DE 5,7 TONNES.
 CETTE FORMATION EST DELIVREE EXCLUSIVEMENT PAR UN INSTRUCTEUR
 DETENTEUR D'UNE QUALIFICATION DE VOL EN MONTAGNE OU PAR UN
INSTRUCTEUR APTE A DELIVRER L'AUTORISATION DE SITE (VOIR ALINEA
 C)).
 LA MENTION D'AUTORISATION D'ACCES A L'AERODROME EST APPOSEE PAR
 L'INSTRUCTEUR SUR LE CARNET DE VOL DU PILOTE OU FORMALISEE SOUS
 LA FORME D'UNE ATTESTATION.
C) L'APTITUDE D'UN INSTRUCTEUR CHARGE DE DELIVRER L'AUTORISATION
 DE SITE EST SUBORDONNEE A UNE FORMATION THEORIQUE AU SOL
 EFFECTUEE PAR:
- UN INSTRCUTEUR DETENTEUR D'UNE QUALIFICATION DE VOL EN
 MONTAGNE OU
- UN INSTRUCTEUR DETENTEUR EN TANT QUE PILOTE DE L'APTITUDE A
 UTILISER L'AERODROME ET FORMALISEE PAR UNE ATTESTATION DE
 FORMATION OU SUR SON CARNET DE VOL OU
- UN INSTRUCTEUR SUR ENTRAINEUR SYNTHETIQUE DE VOL QUI DELIVRE
 CETTE FORMATION D'ACCES A L'AERODROME SUR FSTD.
 CETTE APTITUDE DE L'INSTRUCTEUR VAUT AUTORISATION D'ACCES EN
 QUALITE DE PILOTE.
D) LE MAINTIEN DE L'APTITUDE D'UN PILOTE A UTILISER L'AERODROME
 EST SUBORDONNE A LA REALISATION D'AU MOINS UN ATTERRISSAGE ET
 UN DECOLLAGE EN QUALITE DE COMMANDANT DE BORD DANS LES DOUZE
 DERNIERS MOIS (EXPERIENCE RECENTE EN VOL OU SUR SIMULATEUR DE
 VOL (FSTD)).
E) SI LES CONDITIONS D'EXPERIENCE RECENTE NE SONT PAS REMPLIES,
 LE PILOTE DEVRA DE NOUVEAU REPONDRE A L'UNE DES CONDITIONS A)
 OU B) CI-DESSUS.

 OBBB FIR FOR DESTINATIONS OUTSIDE OBBB FIR SHALL FILE IN ACCORDANCE

APPLICABLE TO DESTINATION.

JEDDAH FIR SHALL FILE VIA NIDAP L550 OR DEKOB P517 OR KATOD G667 OR

ROUTES:

OR H741 ASVIR.

OR DIVERSION
REQUIREMENTS DUE TO TACTICAL REASONS.

Q) TJZS/QAFXX/IV/NBO/E/000/999/1822N06516W999
A) TJZS B) 2503251621 C) PERM
E) FEDERAL AVIATION ADMINISTRATION
SAN JUAN COMBINED CONTROL FACILITY (CCF)
CAROLINA, PR 00979-7421
ISSUED:
SAN JUAN COMBINED CONTROL FACILITY LETTER TO AIRMEN
SUBJECT:  DORADO VFR PRACTICE AREA SAFETY
BACKGROUND:  THE DORADO VFR PRACTICE AREA IS LOCATED IN AN AREA
WHERE HIGH PERFORMANCE JET TRAFFIC MAY BE DESCENDING INTO SAN JUAN
INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT.  THIS POTENTIAL SAFETY RISK REQUIRES THE NEED
FOR INCREASED AWARENESS ON THE PART OF THE PARTICIPANTS DUE TO THE
HIGH VOLUME OF JET TRAFFIC IN AND AROUND THE VFR PRACTICE AREA.
PURPOSE: THE PURPOSE OF THIS LETTER TO AIRMEN IS TO ADVISE ALL
PARTICIPANTS OF THE ESTABLISHMENT OF THE DORADO VFR PRACTICE AREA
(SEE ATTACHMENT) IN SAN JUAN COMBINED CONTROL FACILITY) AIRSPACE,
AND TO INCREASE SAFETY IN THE OPERATIONS IN AND AROUND THIS AREA.
THE PROCEDURES AND AREA DEFINED IN THIS LETTER WERE THE
RECOMMENDATION AGREED TO BY A JOINT COMMITTEE OF LOCAL AREA FLIGHT
SCHOOLS AND THE FAA.
THE DORADO VFR PRACTICE AREA IS DESCRIBED AS THAT AREA BOUNDED ON
THE NORTH BY THE NORTHERN PUERTO RICO COASTLINE (18 DEGREES, 30
MINUTES NORTH), TO THE WEST BY THE TOWN OF PALMAS ALTAS, TO THE
SOUTH BY THE TOWN OF COROZAL, AND TO THE EAST BY THE TOWN OF VEGA
ALTA.  THE VERTICAL LIMITS ARE SURFACE TO 3,000 FEET MSL.
INCREASED AWARENESS MUST BE MAINTAINED BY ALL PARTICIPANTS WHILE
FLYING IN THE PRACTICE AREA DESCRIBED BELOW DUE TO HIGH TRAFFIC
VOLUME, AND OVERFLYING TRANSITIONING JET TRAFFIC, WHERE WAKE
TURBULENCE MAY BE PRESENT.  USE EXTREME CAUTION AND INCREASE OUTSIDE
COCKPIT VIGILANCE.
PROCEDURES:   THE FOLLOWING PROCEDURES WILL RESULT IN INCREASED
SAFETY BY ENSURING VERTICAL SEPARATION FROM OVERFLYING JET TRAFFIC,
ALLEVIATING FREQUENCY CONGESTION, AND IMPROVING PARTICIPANT
AWARENESS OF POTENTIAL CONFLICTING TRAFFIC.
PILOTS TRANSITIONING TO/FROM ISLA GRANDE AIRPORT SHOULD ENTER/EXIT
THE PRACTICE AREA AT OR BELOW 1200 FEET MSL, WHILE REMAINING CLEAR
OF SAN JUAN CLASS C AIRSPACE.
PILOTS OPERATING WITHIN THE PRACTICE AREA SHOULD COMMUNICATE THEIR
RELATIVE POSITIONS TO OTHER PARTICIPANTS ON THE AIR-TO AIR FREQUENCY
122.75 MHZ.
PILOTS OPERATING OUTSIDE THE PRACTICE AREA MAY CONTACT SAN JUAN
APPROACH ON FREQUENCY 119.4, FOR TRAFFIC ADVISORIES.
LOCAL AREA FLIGHT SCHOOLS MAY DEVELOP MORE SPECIFIC PROCEDURES AND
TRAINING FOR THE SAFE OPERATION OF PRACTICE VFR FLIGHT WITHIN THE
PRACTICE AREA, TO RECOMMEND FLIGHT PATHS, ENTRY AND EXIT ROUTES,
ALTITUDES, SAFE PRACTICES, ETC. WHICH SHOULD BE MUTUALLY COORDINATED
AND COMMUNICATED TO ALL PARTICIPATING PILOTS.  PERIODIC ANALYSIS OF
EVENTS AND OPERATIONS RELATED TO THESE PROCEDURES AND ANY RESULTING
CHANGES AND MONITORING OF IMPROVED PROCEDURES WILL SERVE TO
CONTINUALLY ASSURE SAFE OPERATIONS WITHIN THE VFR PRACTICE AREA.

23.2 SCHEDULE FACILITATION IN FORCE:
23.2.1 INTRODUCTION:
SAINT-BARTHELEMY AIRPORT IS AN AIRPORT WITH SCHEDULE FACILITATION
FOR THE WINTER SEASONS, WITHIN THE MEANING OF COMMUNITY REGULATION
95/93 OF 18 JANUARY 1993 AS AMENDED, DESIGNATED AS SUCH BY JOINT
ORDER OF THE MINISTER IN CHARGE OF CIVIL AVIATION AND THE MINISTER
OF OVERSEAS TERRITORIES.
THE FACILITATION PARAMETERS ARE INDICATED ON THE WEBSITE OF THE
COHOR ASSOCIATION.
ANY LANDING AND TAKE-OFF OF A COMMERCIAL AND BUSINESS AVIATION
AIRCRAFT MUST, EXCEPT IN CASES OF FORCE MAJEURE, EMERGENCY LANDINGS,
STATE OR HUMANITARIAN FLIGHTS, BE SUBJECT TO A PRIOR ALLOCATION OF A
SCHEDULE RECOMMENDATION IN THE WINTER SEASON, BY COHOR.
FOR COMMERCIAL AVIATION (CHARTER/SCHEDULED FLIGHTS), EACH FLIGHT
REQUEST, MODIFICATION AND DELETION MUST BE SENT TO COHOR EITHER BY
E-MAIL IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE IATA SSIM CHAPTER 6 STANDARD, OR BY
USING THE WEBSITE E-AIRPORTSLOTS.
AERO HAVING OBTAINED A USERNAME AND PASSWORD BEFOREHAND FROM COHOR.
FOR BUSINESS AVIATION, EACH FLIGHT REQUEST, MODIFICATION AND
DELETION MUST BE OBTAINED THROUGH A GROUND HANDLER LISTED IN AD 2
TFFJ. AD 2.4.
THE CARRIER MUST KEEP ITS FLIGHT REQUESTS UP TO DATE AND ADJUST ITS
FLIGHT SCHEDULE TAKING INTO ACCOUNT THE SCHEDULE RECOMMENDATIONS
PROVIDED BY COHOR.
COHOR MONITORS COMPLIANCE WITH THE SCHEDULE RECOMMENDATIONS.

ENR-1.10.5 IS REPLACED AS FOLLOWING :
1.10.5 SPECIAL PLANNING
1.10.5.1 FLIGHTS TO OR FROM COORDINATED AERODROMES.
1.10.5.1.1 AFFECTED FLIGHTS
SOME AERODROMES ARE CALLED 'SCHEDULE FACILITATED' OR 'COORDINATED'
AS DEFINED IN THE COMMUNITY REGULATION NO. 95/93 OF 18 JANUARY 1993
AS AMENDED. THEY ARE DESIGNATED AS SUCH BY AN ORDER OF THE MINISTER
RESPONSIBLE FOR CIVIL AVIATION. ON A COORDINATED AIRPORT, ANY
LANDING AND TAKE-OFF OF AN
AIRCRAFT IN IFR FLIGHT MUST, EXCEPT IN CASES OF FORCE MAJEURE,
EMERGENCY LANDING, STATE OR HUMANITARIAN FLIGHTS, BE THE SUBJECT OF
A PRIOR ALLOCATION OF AIRPORT SLOT BY THE COHOR ASSOCIATION. AIRPORT
SLOTS MUST BE UPDATED BY AIRCRAFT OPERATORS BASED ON CHANGES TO
THEIR INITIAL APPLICATION.
THE FRENCH CAA (DGAC) HAS SET UP A SYSTEM FOR CHECKING THE
CONSISTENCY BETWEEN THE FLIGHT PLANS SUBMITTED AND THE AIRPORT SLOTS
ALLOCATED BY THE COORDINATOR FOR THESE AIRPORTS. IN ORDER TO
FACILITATE THIS CONTROL, FOR BUSINESS AND GENERAL AVIATION FLIGHTS,
IT IS MANDATORY TO FILL IN FIELD 18 OF
THE FLIGHT PLAN WITH THE IDENTIFICATION NUMBER COMMUNICATED BY COHOR
WHEN ALLOCATING THE CORRESPONDING AIRPORT SLOT.
THE FILING FORMAT IS: RMK/ASL(IDENTIFICATION NUMBER)
THE IDENTIFICATION NUMBER SHALL BE PROVIDED BY THE COORDINATOR WHEN
THE AIRPORT SLOT IS ALLOCATED. IT CONSISTS OF 14 ALPHANUMERIC
CHARACTERS, THE FIRST 4 OF WHICH ARE THE ICAO CODE OF THE AIRPORT
FOR WHICH THE AIRPORT SLOT WAS ISSUED.
EXAMPLE: RMK/ASLLFMDA000000901
IF THE FLIGHT CONNECTS TWO COORDINATED AIRPORTS, THE
IDENTIFICATION NUMBERS ISSUED BY THE COORDINATOR FOR EACH OF THE
AIRPORTS MUST BE ENTERED IN FIELD 18 IN THE FORMAT BELOW:
RMK/ASLLFMND123456789 RMK/ASLLFMDA901234567
BUSINESS AND GENERAL AVIATION FLIGHTS FOR WHICH THE FLIGHT PLAN DOES
NOT INCLUDE AN IDENTIFICATION NUMBER WILL BE CHECKED WITH THE
OPERATOR BY COHOR AND MAY, IF NECESSARY, BE SUSPENDED. A MESSAGE
WILL THEN BE SENT TO THE ORIGINAL ADDRESS OF THE FLIGHT PLAN, ON
BEHALF OF THE FRENCH CAA (DGAC).
FLIGHTS UNDERTAKEN IN VIOLATION OF THE ABOVE-MENTIONED COMMUNITY
REGULATION NO. 95/93 AND ARTICLE R.6321-21 OF THE TRANSPORTS CODE
(FLIGHTS WITHOUT A CORRESPONDING AIRPORT SLOT) ARE SUBJECT TO AN
ADMINISTRATIVE FINE OF 7500 EUROS, DOUBLED IN THE EVENT OF A REPEAT
INFRINGEMENT IN ACCORDANCE WITH
ARTICLE R.160-1 OF THE SAID CODE.

2.SPECIAL PROCEDURE FOR EMERGENCY DESCENT

PIC(PILOT IN COMMAND) HAS THE RIGHT TO CHANGE THE ORIGINALLY

TURN BACK TO THE ORIGINAL ROUTE BY ATC.

REQUIREMENTS, THE PIC SHALL ESTABLISH CONTACT WITH ATC AS SOON AS
POSSIBLE AND STATE THE INTENTION.

ATC PROMPTLY IF REQUIRING RADAR VECTORS TO REJOIN THE ORIGINAL
ROUTE. ATC SHALL CONTINUE TO PROVIDE AIR TRAFFIC SERVICES
CONSIDERING CURRENT TRAFFIC FLOW, AIRSPACE STRUCTURE,
METEOROLOGICAL CONDITIONS AND OTHER AIRSPACE USER ACTIVITIES.

4. OPERATIONAL REQUIREMENTS
4.1 MANNED AIRCRAFT SHALL BE EQUIPPED WITH A SECONDARY
SURVEILLANCE RADAR (SSR) TRANSPONDER OR OTHER SURVEILLANCE
EQUIPMENT OF EQUIVALENT PERFORMANCE, WHICH SHALL REMAIN ACTIVATED

SURVEILLANCE CAPABILITY, FITTED WITH AN AIRBORNE OPERATIONAL

PERFORMANCE, WHICH SHALL REMAIN ACTIVATED THROUGHOUT THE
FLIGHT.
4.2 PILOTS SHALL MAINTAIN CONTINUOUS TWO-WAY COMMUNICATION WITH
AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL (ATC) UNIT. REMOTE PILOTS OF UNMANNED AIRCRAFT
SYSTEM (UAS) SHALL HAVE RELIABLE MEANS FOR TWO-WAY COMMUNICATION
WITH ATC UNIT. IN THE EVENT OF LOSS OF TWO-WAY COMMUNICATION,
PILOTS OR REMOTE PILOTS OF UAS SHALL IMMEDIATELY SET THE SSR
TRANSPONDER CODE FOR RADIO COMMUNICATION FAILURE, AND TAKE ALL
FEASIBLE MEASURES TO OBTAIN ACKNOWLEDGEMENT FROM ATC UNIT.
4.3 PRIOR TO ENTERING THE SPECIAL RESTRICTED AREA, AIRCRAFT MUST
REPORT THEIR SECURITY STATUS (NOTE 3) TO THE ATC UNIT AND
COOPERATE WITH AIRBORNE TARGET RECOGNITION. WHEN NECESSARY,
AIRCRAFT WITHIN THE SPECIAL RESTRICTED AREA SHALL BE SUBJECT TO
AIRBORNE SECURITY VERIFICATION.
4.4 AIRCRAFT SHALL OPERATE STRICTLY IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE
APPROVED FLIGHT PLAN. ANY INTENTION OR ACTION TO DEVIATE FROM THE
FLIGHT PLAN MUST BE REPORTED TO ATC UNIT IN A
TIMELY MANNER AND APPROVED PRIOR TO EXECUTION.
4.5 WHEN CIVIL AIRCRAFT OPERATES BELOW 3,000M (INCLUDED) ABOVE
MEAN SEA LEVEL, THE INDICATED AIRSPEED (IAS) SHOULD NOT EXCEED
450KMH.
NOTE:
1. CALIBRATION FLIGHTS, TEST FLIGHTS, FERRY FLIGHTS, AND
PRODUCTION FLIGHT TESTS SHALL BE MANAGED IN THE SAME MANNER AS
COMMERCIAL FLIGHTS.
2. BUSINESS FLIGHTS REFER TO THOSE FLIGHT ACTIVITIES APPROVED
UNDER RELEVANT PROVISIONS, AND OPERATED ON A NON-SCHEDULE BASIS
WITH NO PASSENGER TICKET FOR THEIR BUSINESS OR ADMINISTRATIVE
ACTIVITIES, ACCORDING TO THE SLOTS AND AIRPORTS OF DEPARTURE AND
ARRIVAL SPECIFIED BY AN INDIVIDUAL USER.
3. THE CONTENT OF SECURITY STATUS REPORT INCLUDES: AIRCRAFT
IDENTIFICATION (FLIGHT NUMBER, OR AIRCRAFT NATIONALITY AND
REGISTRATION MARK), SSR TRANSPONDER CODE, CURRENT POSITION, AND
NORMALITY OF SECURITY STATUS.

APPROACH, THE PILOT SHALL INFORM ATC.
2.4 ATC MAY ISSUE VISUAL APPROACH CLEARANCE AFTER THE PILOTS
REPORT THE PRECEDING ACFT OR THE AIRPORT IN SIGHT.
2.5 AFTER RECEIVING VISUAL APPROACH CLEARANCE, THE ALTITUDE AND
HEADING SHALL BE CONTROLLED BY PILOT. WHEN CONDUCTING A VISUAL
APPROACH TO THE LANDING AIRPORT OR FOLLOWING PRECEDING ACFT, THE
PILOT IS RESPONSIBLE FOR MAINTAINING SAFE SEPARATION BETWEEN THE
ACFT AND GROUND OBSTACLES. AFTER RECEIVING THE VISUAL APPROACH
CLEARANCE TO FOLLOW PRECEDING ACFT, THE PILOT IS RESPONSIBLE FOR
MAINTAINING SAFE SEPARATION BTN PRECEDING ACFT.
3.EMERGENCY PROCEDURES
3.1 CONVERSION AND TERMINATION OF VISUAL APPROACH
3.1.1 DURING A VISUAL APPROACH , IF A VISUAL APPROACH CANNOT BE
COMPLETED DUE TO LOSS OF VISUAL REFERENCE (AIRPORT OR PRECEDING
ACFT), PILOT SHALL INFORM ATC IMMEDIATELY, ATC MAY ASSIST THE
PILOT TO SWITCH TO INSTRUMENT APPROACH,TERMINATION OF VISUAL
APPROACH OR MISSED APPROACH ACCORDING TO THE PILOT'S INTENTION.
3.1.2 THE MISSED APPROACH OF VISUAL APPROACH IS THE SAME AS
RNAV ILS/DME Z MISSED APPROACH PROCEDURE OF THE LANDING RWY, OR
FOLLOW
ATC CLEARANCE.
3.2 COMMUNICATION FAILURE
3.2.1 IF LANDING CLEARANCE HAS BEEN RECEIVED AT THE TIME OF
COMMUNICATION FAILURE,THE PILOT MAY CONTINUE APPROACH AND LAND.
3.2.2 IF COMMUNICATION
FAILS AT BASE LEG, THE PILOT MAY INTERCEPT
FINAL, CONTINUE VISUAL APPROACH OR SWITCH TO OTHER APPROACH
PROCEDURE.
3.2.3 FOR OTHER COMMUNICATION FAILURE SITUATIONS, THE PILOT MAY
FLW THE PUBLISHED GENERAL PROCEDURES FOR AIR-GROUND TWO-WAY RADIO
COMMUNICATION FAILURE UNDER INSTRUMENT FLIGHT RULES.
